newsitem.title: GERMANY: ROTHFOS DETAILS WORLD COFFEE OUTPUT FORECASTS.
newsitem.headline: ROTHFOS DETAILS WORLD COFFEE OUTPUT FORECASTS.

text.p: Global coffee output in 1997/98 is forecast at 100 million bags, rounded, compared with a revised estimate of 99.3 million bags for 1996/97, figures from German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH showed.
Rothfos said American milds in 1997/98 should account for 34.0 million bags, showing a 1.98 million bag increase over the 1996/97 figure.
African and Asian milds output should also increase due to better East African crops, with 7.26 million bags targeted for 1997/98 after 6.5 million in 1996/97.
Unwashed arabica crops should be down at 24.6 million bags in 1997/98 from 28.6 million in 1996/97, mostly due to a lower Brazilian crop.
Robusta output in 1997/98 was forecast at 34.1 million bags, compared with 32.1 million in 1996/97, with a recovery in Indonesian output cited as one reason.
Output in 1996/97 had been estimated at 97.0 million bags in Rothfos' May estimate.
The latest rise reflected upward revisions in American milds and robustas while other milds and unwashed arabicas were practically unchanged, it said.
